problem: The mechanism is described wrongly. The threshold is not 'outcome-adapted'. Feedback-guided Threshold Adaptation looks at the expert's first Δ actions after takeover: if they reverse the robot's preceding motion, the threshold drops (ask earlier); if they agree with what the policy would have done, it rises (ask later). Separately, the simulation 'expert' is a scripted oracle and 'HG-DAgger' is a rule that imitates human gating. The sim/real labeling is already right. The numbers are correct: SC-Green pi0.5 success BC 49, HG 29, Ours 81, and best in 13 of 15 settings for success (I counted: it loses only on pi0.5 PickPlane and X-VLA SC-Green).
evidence: Sec IV-B2: 'FTA uses the first Δ expert actions after takeover to assess whether assistance was requested too early or too late' ... corrective reversal -> advance (lower threshold); policy-expert agreement -> postpone. Sec V-A4: 'A task-specific oracle replaces human control ... a predefined failure-triggered rule approximates human takeover for Human-Gated DAgger.' Table I pi0.5 SC-Green success: BC 49, HG 29, Diff 34, Ours 81. Sec V-B1: 'highest reported AUPRC, TASR, and post-training success in 13 settings for each metric.'
proposed_fields: {"one_line": "Robot-gated DAgger: asks for takeover when a PCA residual on VLA features exceeds a threshold that the expert's first actions after takeover raise or lower. pi0.5 StackCube-Green (ManiSkill sim, oracle expert): 81 vs HG-DAgger 29, Offline BC 49; best in 13/15 settings."}

problem: 'Collects data with a frozen pi0.5 copy' is misleading. The rollout policy is held fixed only during one update group, then re-synced to the learner after every group (20 critic + 5 actor updates). It is not frozen across training. The numbers check out: RAPolicy mean (100+95+70+80)/4 = 86.25%; EXPO-FT mean (80+80+30+10)/4 = 50%, which matches the paper's stated 72.5% relative improvement. The code link is the paper's official repo, linked from the project page.
evidence: Sec III-A: 'After each group, the rollout policy is synchronized with the learner and remains fixed until the next synchronization. In practice, each update group consists of 20 critic and 5 actor updates, enabling frequent updates to the rollout policy.' Table I (20 trials/task): EXPO-FT 80/80/30/10%, RAPolicy 100/95/70/80%. Paper uses 'IQL-style chunk-value backups'.
proposed_fields: {"one_line": "A rollout copy of pi0.5, re-synced after each update group, collects data while the learner trains an IQL-style chunk critic and a one-step flow actor only on stored actions. Real, 4 tasks: 86.3% average vs EXPO-FT 50%."}

problem: Calling the subject 'RECAP-style advantages' is a mismatch. The paper studies critic-derived advantage-guided post-training in general. It keeps an IQL critic with n-step TD, finds the Monte Carlo value fitting that RECAP uses weaker, and leaves RECAP out as a condition on purpose. Also, the 'DAgger' baseline is not an interactive DAgger run. It is a source-based weighting of the same dataset: human samples get weight 1, autonomous rollouts get 0. Only the reward-level penalty (squared distance to the frozen ACT's actions) anchors to BC. (2) There is no 'small Gaussian head'. The CVAE is removed and the full ACT decoder output becomes the mean of a diagonal Gaussian with learnable log-std. The numbers (sim, 50 episodes) are correct.

'Actor weights' is fine; the paper says 'policy parameters'.
evidence: arXiv 2507.10030 Sec. 4.1: the swing-up time score is 'the earliest timestep such that the pole tip remains within a 0.1-unit radius'. 'We train 10 independent agents.' 'Initially, the average swing-up times are 2.085 s for SAC ... SAC+SNES achieves an average swing-up time of 1.135 s' and 'continuing training with SAC ... for an additional 1000 episodes results in higher swing-up times of 1.565 s'. Sec. 4.2.3: SNES is fine-tuned 'directly on the competition score (13)' for the double pendulum. Affiliation University of Padova verified.
proposed_fields: {"one_line": "Pretrains SAC on a dense surrogate reward, then fine-tunes the policy weights with SNES using the true task score as fitness. Sim cartpole swing-up time (mean of 10 agents): 2.085 s → 1.135 s, vs 1.565 s after 1000 more SAC-only episodes."}

short: Diffusion Policies with Value-Conditional Optimization for Offline Reinforcement Learning
problem: The mechanism is described wrongly. DIVO does not condition on anything. It weights the diffusion training loss with binary advantage weights, and the diffusion model is a behavior model, not the deployed policy. The learned policy is a separate TD3+BC actor that is regularized toward diffusion samples with non-negative advantage. Family: this is a pure D4RL offline-RL paper with no robot manipulation, so it fits 'generalrl' ('Not robot-manipulation papers ... flow/diffusion policy theory') better than advbc. The 'short' field holds the full title instead of the method name.
evidence: arXiv 2511.08922 Eq. 9-10: L_PAD = E[f(s,a)·||eps − eps_omega||^2], f(s,a)=eta·1(Q_phi(s,a)−V_psi(s)). Sec. III-B: 'Within ADPO, the diffusion model serves as the behavior policy rather than the learned policy'; Eq. 12 target = pi_omega(s) if A(s,pi_omega(s))>=0; Eq. 13 actor loss −alpha·Q + beta·||pi_theta − pi_target||^2; 'Our algorithm is built upon the TD3+BC framework'. Abstract: evaluated on D4RL locomotion and AntMaze; comment field: IROS 2025.
proposed_fields: {"one_line": "DIVO (IROS 2025): trains a diffusion behavior model with binary advantage-based loss weights, then regularizes a TD3+BC actor toward diffusion samples with non-negative advantage; reports gains on D4RL locomotion and AntMaze.", "family": "generalrl", "short": "DIVO"}

problem: The phrase 'making PPO's ratio exact' is not a claim the paper makes, and it misdescribes the mechanism. Both v1 (DMPO) and v2 (OGPO) write the policy as a noise-injected Gaussian Markov chain whose joint log-probability is tractable for any K steps, the same idea DPPO/ReinFlow use. v2 says only that K=1 gives 'low-variance policy gradients'. So one-step generation is not what makes the ratio exact. The numbers check out: Square 0.83 at 1 NFE vs DPPO 0.78 at 20 NFE (Table 1, 100-trajectory MH data). The BC-ablation collapse to near zero is in v1 Appendix A.3.2. Org SYSU and code repo ogpo-project/OGPO are verified.

Square 0.78'; 'OGPO (Ours) | 1 | ... 0.83'. v1 App. A.3.2: 'without BC regularization, the success rate rapidly collapses to near zero across all runs'.
